headline: New law orders a study of cancer rates and cancer deaths among veterans who served as military aircrew on fixed-wing planes.
what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to make an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. The National Academies will study how common cancers are, and how often they cause death, among certain veterans. The study covers veterans who served on active duty as aircrew members and regularly flew in fixed-wing aircraft, and the results must be reported.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who served as aircrew on fixed-wing military aircraft
who_it_affects.how: Their cancer rates and cancer deaths will be studied, which could inform future VA policies.
The VA must set up and pay for an agreement with the National Academies to carry out the study.

who_it_affects.group: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
who_it_affects.how: The organization will conduct the study and report its findings.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted August 14, 2025; the summary does not give deadlines for the study or report.
